newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TWO UNITEDS BEMOAN FRAILTY OF HUMAN ANKLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO UNITEDS BEMOAN FRAILTY OF HUMAN ANKLE.

text.p: Manchester United and Newcastle United kick off the new season at the weekend also united by the frailty of the human ankle.
The top two clubs in English soccer last season are both missing their main target men due to injuries suffered over the summer break.

Alan Shearer, top striker last season for Newcastle with 25 premier league goals, is likely to be out until well into the New Year after fracturing his ankle on wet grass in a friendly against Chelsea.
Norwegian Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Manchester United's leading target man with 18 goals, is also out with a lesser ankle injury suffered at the end of July in a friendly against Internazionale Milan.
He could be back by the end of the month, although a spokeswoman could give no provisional date.
The injuries rob the start of the season of two of the most prolific and natural scorers in England.
But the missing men do not end there.
Half the leading 12 scorers -- and three of the top four -- from last season are sidelined or absent from Saturday's kickoff.
Liverpool's Robbie Fowler (18 goals) and Southampton's Matthew Le Tissier (13) are the others missing through injury.

Another has fled -- Juninho (12) of relegated Middlesbrough to Spain -- while former club mate Fabrizio Ravanelli (16) starts the season as the only Italian international in the English first division.
Remarkably, of the leading 12 league goalscorers from 1996-97, only four are still at last season's clubs.
Les Ferdinand, Newcastle's second most prolific scorer, has been sold to Tottenham while Liverpool's Stan Collymore (12) has gone to Aston Villa.
Only the Arsenal duo of Ian Wright (23 goals) and Dennis Bergkamp (12), Aston Villa's Dwight Yorke (17) and Leicester's Steve Claridge (12) have stayed put.
With some of the leading target men as spectators, foreign feet are sure to find the goals with Chelsea's Italian Gianfranco Zola a prime candidate.
Manchester United, with one of the strongest squads in the country and a bevy of leading internationals, can afford to be philosophical -- although they have also lost their chief philosopher.
Some would undoubtedly say that, even if Man Utd see off all opponents with the deftest of flicks and most balletic of dances, the poetry will be blanker verse.
Translated, that means no more Marseillaise, no more turned-up collars and no more musings from Eric Cantona.
When Sunday comes, it will also bring United's first league match since the gifted one retired.
Eric -- "Ooh Aah", EC or just God -- the moody Gallic artist renowned for his penchant for the verses of Rimbaud and acrobatic karate-kicks, has said au revoir.

With the ocean of life outside football clearly offering greater attractions for Eric than Old Trafford on a wet and wintery weekend, United fans need a new "Dieu" to command their affection and admiration.
Which is where Teddy Sheringham steps up.

The 31-year-old England striker was signed from Tottenham Hotspur over the summer for around $5.7 million as the turbulent Frenchman's replacement and is one attacker set to make more of a mark this season.

England manager Glenn Hoddle certainly believes that Sheringham could be the man to take United to the international glory that the club craves and that the departed Frenchman was never able to deliver.
"When I saw the Charity Shield on Sunday, I thought Teddy Sheringham had played there for six or seven years," Hoddle told reporters on Tuesday.
"Eric Cantona for all the great things he's done for United, wasn't playing international football."
Manager Alex Ferguson said that Sheringham was a "direct replacement for Eric", adding that he is "not a replica but there is a likeness between the two."
Despite four league titles in the past five years, Manchester United yearn to lay their hands on the European Cup again for the first time since 1968.
That is the grail for any Man Utd boss. For Newcastle ones, the first league title since 1927 would do, although the injury to Shearer makes that quest look more difficult than a few months ago.
Different titles, but the same determination.
